questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.
Stop and rest off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
Other drivers will notice you if you turn your head.
You should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in handling may mean a tire has failed. Pull over safely and check your tires if your motorcycle feels different.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs show road rules that riders must follow.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your system.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your system.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your riding ability.

questions.question: During daytime riding, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you choose to.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face
Your face, but not your eyes

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses are not adequate protection for either.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as they may catch the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off other vehicles.
The one that allows other motorists to see you.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows other motorists to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. This position also helps you see others, avoid wind blasts and blind spots, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What must you have when carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat that is large enough for two riders.
You should not require the passenger to wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: What should you do while riding?

options.text: Always scan ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Do not worry about hazards because they are minimal.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always scan ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead on the road to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: What should you check about your brakes during a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: They make a loud squeaking noise.
They cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit to give the best protection?

options.text: It can have a few cracks.
It does not need to be certified.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards. It should fit snugly all around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to avoid problems. Small technical issues on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. Change lanes safely and let them get in front of you. Riding faster will only make it more dangerous.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. A car may pull out from the curb or leave a parking space without warning.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose so they flap in the wind.
Only cover part of your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright colors helps other drivers see you. Choose clothes that make you visible during the day and at night.
